$comment: 🔮️ Test-only third-party references of the repo workspace module. Both packages are devDependencies of 📦️packages/🟦️typescript and are imported only from 🧪️tests/**; no runtime code may depend on either.

oracles.rationale: A widely used glob engine decides what each pattern means, so the owned regular-expression translation cannot agree with itself about `**`, character classes or segment boundaries.
A gitignore-conformant matcher decides precedence, directory rules and negation for the vector set the owned matcher claims to agree with git on.

noOracleDecisions.rationale: Repository-root discovery, the `.🧬semio` layout vocabulary and the `📋️config.toml` reader are this repository's own conventions. Nothing third party knows that a semio monorepo root is recognised by a legacy CLI entry point, then a git checkout, then a Go module, or that `[logging] detail` has three levels. Confidence comes from specification vectors materialised into a work-directory tree plus two independently written implementations.

The owned matcher accepts the POSIX `[!…]` character-class negation spelling, which picomatch — and therefore micromatch — reads as a literal class containing an exclamation mark. Inside a negated class every member is literal, so `[!a-c]` excludes the three characters and the hyphen rather than a range. A picomatch-based oracle disagrees by construction, so this spelling is held by the two subjects agreeing with the recorded expectation instead.

Two rule shapes are deliberately NOT git-compatible: a leading slash is not treated as a root anchor, and a negation can re-include a file underneath an excluded directory. A gitignore-conformant oracle disagrees by construction, so these two vectors are held by the two subjects agreeing with each other and with the recorded expectation instead.
